By default, Heading styles are set to a medium variable, but there are two other sizes if you’d prefer a different value.

To change it, you can edit the style and change the variable that the style points to.

Most systems have a requirement for a text style with 100% (or 1) line height, which means creating more Figma styles. In code, things are treated differently.

We have created a text style group called Single Line, which at the moment contains two styles: a body base, and a small variant with strong font weight.

This is something we are likely to reconsider in the future.

To theme the Simple Design System to look like your brand:

Go to the Color Primitives collection and find the group Brand.
Change the hex values in this group to match your brand’s color ramp.
The Colors collection will automatically update:
Background
Border
Icon
Text

To change the Space variables of the Simple Design System to look like your brand:

Go to the Size collection
Change the raw values of the variables to match your brand’s style

Simple Design System’s approach to Padding and Gap is to consolidate them into a single Space variable group which can be applied in any field.
To change the effects within the Simple Design System to look like your brand, change the values stored within each Style.

The following documentation is provided as a guide for developers. There are no grid styles/settings within Figma as we rely solely on auto layout for grid definitions. 

These rules are all represented in Storybook.

––

Simple Design System relies on Flex for the layout system. 

There are two components:

Flex
FlexItem

Flex can be a container, which snaps its widths responsively.

By default, any child of Flex is an item, but explicit child layouts are created using FlexItems.

Flex components can be aligned to a grid that we define as:

Auto
Quarter
Third
Half grids

FlexItems can be set to:

Minor
Major
Half
Full

These change at breakpoints, becoming full width on mobile.

Flex components must explicitly set to wrap.
Quarter or thirds on tablet
Full width on mobile

Sections span the full page width.


They have fixed x axis padding and variable y axis padding.


You can horizontally align content any way you would like inside of a section.


Sections can either be <header>, <footer>, or HTML <section> elements.


Sections can have a brand background color (primary, secondary, tertiary), a subtle bg-secondary background.


Sections can be bordered, but there are guidelines. They can have a top and bottom border, unless they are the first or last child respectively.


For multi-column inner content, alignment is set to left.


For single vertically aligned inner content, the alignment is set to centre.

Title#348:1.value:
Images are not created as components in Figma, but exist as components in code.

Size is applied to the max height.

Images scale to that height at the provided aspect ratio.

Aspect ratios fix the image sizes regardless of its natural dimensions, covering the object and positioned in the centre.
“Fill” preserves the aspect ratio while scaling 100% horizontally.
“Natural” size does not attempt to scale the image, but has a max-width of 100%.

Figma supports text decoration overrides, but we recommend using variables for:

Bold / Strong
Italic / Emphasis

Text style overrides are great for body text, but not entire strings.
